t:
The budgetary effects of this Act, for the purpose of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this Act, submitted for printing in the 
Congressional Record by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee, provided that such statement has been submitted prior to the vote on passage.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a statement "submitted" before a "vote" is a procedural input into a decision. But the only actor is the Chairman of the House Budget Committee, a member of Congress, and the vote is a legislative vote on passage, so everything stays inside the federal government. This is standard PAYGO budget-scoring boilerplate, with no public comment, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: Congressional Record by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee, provided that such statement has been submitted prior to the vote on passage.

qwen_block.w: This section describes a procedural requirement for submitting a budgetary statement to the Congressional Record by a member of Congress (the Chairman of the House Budget Committee). Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. There is no consultation with or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_block.s: submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee

opus.w: This is standard PAYGO compliance boilerplate. It only says how the Act's budgetary effects are measured: by a statement from the Chairman of the House Budget Committee. Congress and its committee chairs are inside the federal government, so no outside party is consulted or involved. The procedural wording might seem to suggest participation, but none of it reaches anyone outside the government.
opus.s:
submitted for printing in the 
Congressional Record by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee
opus.b: **Step 1 – Analysis.** One could misread this as participation because it describes a formal procedure: a statement gets submitted for printing in the Congressional Record. But everyone involved is inside the federal government. The Chairman of the House Budget Committee is a member of Congress, and the statement is used to apply a federal budget-scoring law. This is standard PAYGO boilerplate, and no outside party takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a procedural rule for determining budgetary effects by referencing a statement from the Chairman of the House Budget Committee. The Chairman is a member of Congress, which is considered inside the federal government. There is no consultation with or participation by entities outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private organizations).
qwen_chat.s: The budgetary effects of this Act, for the purpose of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this Act, submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that referencing a statement submitted by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee involves an outside party, but the Chairman is a member of Congress, which is inside the federal government. Furthermore, this is a procedural rule for budget scoring, not a mechanism for public or external consultation on a policy decision.
